5fe631f3bb5b: FullCalendar in Salesforce vs MultiDatePick: Which LWC Calendar Is More Customizable?
364324573707: FullCalendar in Salesforce vs MultiDatePick: views, drag and drop, field colors, custom objects, filters and booking rules compared, plus when FullCalendar wins.
babdfe982745: What is the most customizable LWC calendar for Salesforce?
e8edb5522e54: It depends on who does the customizing. FullCalendar's LWC wrapper gives developers the most freedom, because everything is code. MultiDatePick gives admins the most built-in options: more than 130 settings across three components, five views and six ways to save records, all without Apex.
38c6c833a0be: The core library is open source. The timeline and resource views are Premium features that need a commercial license, and the Salesforce side (loading records, saving, security and tests) is code you write and maintain.
68ec2d81dfc9: Does MultiDatePick need Apex or a developer?
b1aefd5925d6: No. You set it up in the Setup Wizard or in Lightning App Builder, on any standard or custom object. Records load and save as the viewing user, with sharing and field-level security applied.
df1f1b1d4d18: Can MultiDatePick show Tasks, Events and Opportunities?
35c18896b253: Yes. Any object with a Date or Date/Time field works, standard or custom. A Rollup Field adds records that point to the page record from further away, such as tasks on an account's contacts.
3f58a269e6ae: Does MultiDatePick include a resource timeline?
c35c8f925733: Yes. Timeline, week, utilization heatmap and agenda views are included with the calendar, with no extra license. One plan has every feature.
34ec4d1e1767: One is a JavaScript calendar engine you build on. The other is a Salesforce calendar you configure. Here is every item on the usual "customizable calendar" checklist, side by side, including where FullCalendar is the better pick.
900ff834403c: Ask for "a super customizable LWC calendar for Salesforce" and two names come up again and again: FullCalendar, the open-source JavaScript calendar that now ships an official Lightning Web Component wrapper, and MultiDatePick, a native calendar and booking suite. Both are called customizable. They mean very different things by it.
5fbf60902844: <t1>FullCalendar</t1> customizes through code: you pass an options object, write callbacks, and build the Salesforce side yourself (the Apex that loads records, the save, the permissions). <t2>MultiDatePick</t2> customizes through settings: more than 130 of them across its three components, set in a Setup Wizard or in Lightning App Builder, on any standard or custom object. <t3>No Apex required.</t3>

b8854d312321: Where FullCalendar is the better choice
4a2900ce1a56: FullCalendar earns its reputation, and for some projects it is the right tool:
5a5c651b51ef: You need a view type nobody ships, such as a quarterly planning board or a custom dispatch layout.
5b8dbf7ee501: You want to draw each event pixel by pixel, with your own HTML and icons inside the bar.
7f4702b2834b: Your events come from outside Salesforce, from several APIs at once.
e1d23947f162: You have developers to build the Apex, the save, the tests and the permissions, and to maintain them.
535400347bf0: You only need to display events and want the free core library.
451b92195ec4: If that is your project, FullCalendar is a fine foundation. If what you need is a calendar that works on your Salesforce records this week, it is a long way from the finish line.
7e1d04979442: The work FullCalendar leaves to you is the work MultiDatePick ships:
8bd54d3a9894: Scattered days, ranges and recurring patterns, saved as child records or passed to a Screen Flow.
f2ca85526965: Live capacity badges, conflict checks on save and several resources in one booking.
b5cceb26d069: Notice, booking window, buffers, business hours and closures, enforced on pick and on drag.
201f78050f5c: Three questions about your records, then every setting with a live preview of the real calendar.
36fc94724076: Selected dates, ranges and times come out as Flow variables for your next steps.
33fa422026dc: Experience Cloud sites with guest users, the same calendar and the same rules.
5fbf2ca3b58c: MultiDatePick is known for booking, but it is also a calendar for records you already have. Put it on an Account page and show the account's tasks, including those on its contacts and opportunities. Show opportunity close dates, campaign event days or project milestones on any object. Turn on <t1>Show All Records</t1> with a record filter such as <t2>OwnerId=ME</t2> for a personal calendar, or use the read-only Agenda and Utilization views to watch the schedule without editing it.
